<thought>To meet the three‑step limit, I selected a convergent route that uses only commercially available, inexpensive reagents.  
Step 1 – Sulfonamide formation: p‑toluidine (4‑methyl‑aniline) reacts with 4‑bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give the aryl‑bromide sulfonamide. The retrosynthetic template for this transformation is reaction ID 733 (amine + sulfonyl chloride → sulfonamide).  
Step 2 – Suzuki coupling: The bromide on the sulfonamide is coupled with (E)‑3‑(N‑phenyl)acrylic acid pinacol ester (a vinyl‑boronate) to install the trans‑vinyl amide side chain. The retrosynthetic template for this C–C bond‑forming Suzuki reaction is reaction ID 300317 (aryl bromide + vinyl‑boronate → substituted alkene).  
All three starting materials – p‑toluidine, 4‑bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, and (E)‑3‑(N‑phenyl)acrylic acid pinacol ester – are commercially available, and their combined cost is far below the $9 999 budget. The route consists of only two synthetic steps (well within the ≤3‑step limit).
